module_title: Intermediate Office Shortcuts - Alignment, Search, and Hyperlinks
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on paragraph alignment in Word, search-and-replace mechanics, and specific foundational Excel navigation shortcuts frequently tested in Banking and SSC exams.

core_concepts.title: Paragraph Alignment (MS Word)
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + L`: Align text to the Left.
- `Ctrl + R`: Align text to the Right.
- `Ctrl + E`: Align text to the Center.
- `Ctrl + J`: Justify text (aligns evenly along both left and right margins).

core_concepts.title: Search and Edit
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + F`: Open the 'Find' navigation pane to search for words.
- `Ctrl + H`: Open the 'Replace' dialog box (Find and Replace).

core_concepts.title: Crucial Insertions
core_concepts.description:
- `Ctrl + K`: Insert a Hyperlink (clickable web link).
- `F7`: Run the Spelling and Grammar check.

core_concepts.title: Basic Excel Selectors
core_concepts.description:
- `Shift + Spacebar`: Select the entire Row in Excel.
- `Ctrl + Spacebar`: Select the entire Column in Excel.
- `Alt + Enter`: Start a new line inside the SAME cell (Wrap Text).

important_entities.name: F7 Key
important_entities.significance: Pressing `F7` anywhere in MS Office instantly opens the Spelling and Grammar checker. It is one of the most repeatedly asked function key questions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'What is the shortcut to Center align text?' Do NOT pick `Ctrl + C`. `Ctrl + C` is already reserved for Copy. Center alignment strictly uses `Ctrl + E`.
Similar to the above, do NOT pick `Ctrl + H` for Hyperlink. `Ctrl + H` is reserved for 'Replace'. Hyperlink strictly uses `Ctrl + K`.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To remember that `Ctrl + K` is for inserting links, focus on the last letter of the word 'HyperlinK'.

exam_strategy_tips: Memorize `Ctrl + E` (Center Alignment) and `Ctrl + K` (Hyperlink) perfectly. They appear in almost every SSC CGL and Banking Computer Knowledge question bank due to their non-intuitive letters.
